cues.text: Next, sleeves and shirts. Sleeve length is easy to pin once you know where it should end.
The customer stands with arms relaxed at their sides.
A jacket sleeve should show a little shirt cuff, about a quarter to a half inch.
A shirt sleeve ends at the wrist bone, where the hand begins.
Fold the extra up inside the sleeve, to the right length.
Use two pins, one on the top and one underneath.
Do both arms. Most people have one arm a little longer.
Look at the cuff buttons. Jacket sleeves with working buttonholes are hard to shorten. Write it on the ticket for the tailor.
If a shirt is too wide, pinch the same amount on both side seams, and pin up and down from the underarm to the bottom.
Ask the customer to lift their arms. It should still feel comfortable.
